item.title: Amazon, Walmart Face Data Requests in DOJ Beef Antitrust Probe
item.description: The US Justice Department expanded its antitrust inquiry of the meatpacking industry by demanding information on surging beef prices from eight major food retailers, including Amazon.com Inc., Costco Wholesale Corp. and Walmart Inc.

item.title: Kalshi Seeks Never-Expiring Oil Futures Amid 24/7 Trading Debate
item.description: Kalshi Inc. will seek regulatory approval for an oil-linked futures contract that never expires, a move that would bring a product popular in crypto markets into the traditional energy sphere as the industry debates the risks of round-the-clock markets.

item.title: Napster Shifts Course to Penny-a-Minute AI Agents Via Microsoft
item.description: Napster, the former music-streaming platform, is betting on low-cost AI agents as its path back to success.

item.title: UVA’s Situational Awareness Bet Fueled Record Year Before Tumult
item.description: When AI-focused hedge fund Situational Awareness lost more than two-thirds of its $45 billion in July, most of the investors who took the hit were wealthy individuals and tech founders.

item.title: Iran-linked Hackers Hit 100 American Water Utilities
item.description: EPA giving away $11 million to boost water systems cybersecurity

item.title: Uber’s $15 Billion Delivery Hero Takeover Gains Board Backing
item.description: Delivery Hero SE’s board voted to accept a takeover offer from Uber Technologies Inc., moving the nearly $15 billion deal for the German delivery platform another step toward completion.

item.title: NYSE Used Anthropic’s Project Glasswing to Find Cyber Flaws
item.description: The New York Stock Exchange used Anthropic PBC’s Project Glasswing to find and fix vulnerabilities in its cyber security systems, its president, Lynn Martin, told Congress.

item.title: Fed Watchdog Flags Questions Around Confidential Information
item.description: The Federal Reserve’s internal watchdog said the central bank should do more to prevent the sharing of confidential nonpublic information with its 12 regional reserve bank boards, which include private-sector bankers and business leaders.

item.title: US Lawmakers Pass Africa Trade Preference Extension to 2028
item.description: US lawmakers agreed to extend a trade preference program with African nations until the end of 2028.

item.title: Circle K Owner Says Inflation, Fuel Costs Curb Consumer Spending
item.description: Convenience and gas station retailer Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. reported record fuel sales as oil prices soared amid the Middle East conflict, but consumers are also tightening their budgets and visiting stores less often. Shares dropped the most in more than five months.

item.title: Fashion Empire Azzas 2154 to Split Two Years After Failed Merger
item.description: Azzas 2154 SA, one of Brazil’s largest apparel exporters, will split into two independent publicly traded companies as its main shareholders seek to end a months-long dispute over governance and strategy.

item.title: Uber to Exit Nigeria, Uganda as Part of Global Restructure
item.description: US ride-hailing giant Uber Technologies Inc. is shutting down its services in Nigeria and Uganda from September 2, following a global review of its operations.

item.title: Senegal’s Bond Selloff Reveals Investor Angst on Debt Rework
item.description: Investors who had been holding out hope that Senegal could avoid a default are changing tack, selling its short-dated bonds as they expect losses ahead.

item.title: Danish Central Bank Intervenes Again to Defend Currency Peg
item.description: Denmark’s central bank intervened to support a weakening krone for the second time since June, underscoring the persistent pressure on the currency that could herald an interest-rate hike.

item.title: Spyware Targeted Serbian Protest Organizers’ Phones, Report Says
item.description: Spyware targeted Serbian student activists and politicians involved in anti-corruption protests against President Aleksandar Vucic ahead of local elections in March, a new report claimed.

item.title: The ‘Permission Bottleneck’ Coming for Stocks
item.description: The AI buildout has been lifting all boats.

item.title: AI Startup Wonderful Raises Funds at $5 Billion Valuation
item.description: Wonderful has closed a fundraising round that values the Israeli-Dutch startup, which builds software that coordinates artificial intelligence agents, at $5 billion.

item.title: Italy’s Eni Plans Major Increase in Venezuela Oil Production
item.description: Italian energy producer Eni SpA aims to eventually lift its Venezuelan production to more than 1 million barrels a day, according to people familiar with the matter, a figure that includes volumes from state-owned Petróleos de Venezuela SA and would bolster US efforts to revive the country’s battered oil industry.

item.title: Google Avoids Breakup as Judge Orders Ad Tech Unit Changes
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google doesn’t have to sell off its advertising exchange and instead must make its ad tech tools work with those operated by rivals, a federal judge ruled Wednesday, in a move that saves the tech giant from a second bid to force a breakup.

item.title: Bessent Leaves BOJ in No-Win Situation Over Japan Rate Hikes
item.description: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda faces unusually acute risks of financial-market turbulence as he approaches this month’s policy decision in the wake of a public pressure campaign by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

item.title: S&P 500 Gains After Three-Day Skid as Oil Prices Halt Advance
item.description: US stocks turned positive after flipping between small gains and losses earlier in Wednesday’s session, as oil prices halted a sharp advance, easing inflation concerns as traders weigh the Federal Reserve’s potential path for interest-rate hikes.

item.title: Yen Surges With Traders on Alert for Further Intervention
item.description: The yen strengthened sharply against the US dollar, leaving traders hyper-vigilant for evidence that authorities are taking further action to support the Japanese currency.

item.title: Bank of Canada Holds Rates and Flags Inflation Risks; Bonds Drop
item.description: The Bank of Canada held interest rates steady for a seventh consecutive meeting, but emphasized that an escalation of the trade war with the US and the Iran conflict are fueling new inflation concerns.

item.title: Upwind Raises $300 Million at $3.8 Billion Valuation for AI, Cloud Cybersecurity
item.description: Upwind Security, a startup offering cybersecurity for artificial intelligence and cloud applications, is raising fresh financing that values the company at $3.8 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Spain’s Push on Undocumented Migrants Distorts Labor Statistics
item.description: Spain’s decision to grant residency permits to undocumented migrants is reshaping its labor-market data, bringing more workers onto formal payrolls while simultaneously pushing up the number registered as jobless.

item.title: Fed’s Warsh Lays Out Data Dashboard to Read US Economy
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh used his keynote speech in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, last week to map out some of the key data points he leans on to read the US economy, offering new insight into his approach to policy making.

item.title: EU Moves to Support Ukraine Grain Exports and Shield Farmers
item.description: The European Union is looking “at all possible lanes” to support grain exports from Ukraine and is working to blunt the financial impact of extreme weather on farmers as part of a responsibility to safeguard global food supply, according to the bloc’s agriculture commissioner.

item.title: Nvidia’s Huang Urges G20 to Speed AI Adoption as Key to Growth
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang called on Group of 20 nations to accelerate their adoption of artificial intelligence as a way to enhance growth, urging the world’s largest economies to expand data centers and other infrastructure to support the emerging technology.

item.title: ElevenLabs Hires OpenAI VP as First Chief Revenue Officer
item.description: ElevenLabs has hired former OpenAI executive Ashley Kramer as its first chief revenue officer, part of the startup’s efforts to drum up business demand for its artificial intelligence voice tools.

item.title: Fed’s Williams Says Inflation Continuing to Trend Down
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said there’s evidence inflation continues to ease as the impact of tariffs fades while higher energy prices are not spreading to other services.
